# Skins — global skin pack for DeepSeek Harness
[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@fanfan4589/dsh-skins) [](./LICENSE)
A skin switcher **inside Settings**, not the sidebar: two global palettes for DeepSeek Harness, swit
ched in one click, with no feature changes.
中文
| Paper (default, light) | Ink (dark) |
## Usage
**Settings → General → Skin** (between “Language” and “Appearance”):
| Choice | Result |

| Paper | Ivory `#faf9f5`, beige sidebar, warm ink `#1f1e1b`, terracotta `#c96442` |
| Ink | Charcoa

l `#181818`, warm neutral greys, terracotta accent |
| Off | Restores the shipped DSH theme |
| Afte
r switching | Applies instantly; survives reload and restart (`localStorage: dsh-skins:active`) |
Each skin ships both a light and a dark palette, so **Settings → Appearance** (light / dark / system
) still applies. The skin only owns colour; it does not take over the appearance preference.
## How it works
- **Token-only**: each skin re-points ~106 `--dsw-*` design variables (palette ramps, semantic alias

es, scenario tokens). No component replacement, no DOM reads, no feature changes.
- **Reading comfor
t**: body text keeps the highest contrast; tool rows, timestamps and telemetry step back through `se

condary / tertiary / caption`; hairlines fade; content leading +1px.
- **Cold-start safe**: selector
s sit one step above the base sheets (`html[data-dsh-skin="paper"] body…`), so the host’s later-inje

cted base styles cannot override the skin.
- **One stylesheet**: switching only moves the `<html dat
a-dsh-skin>` attribute — no style rebuild, no page reload.

## Compatibility

- Requires `dsh >= 0.2.1-rc.1` (web client).
- On macOS the sidebar is system vibrancy (the shipped
CSS makes it transparent under `[data-platform=darwin]`), so its base colour is the OS material; tok

ens still control the sidebar’s inner elements and every non-darwin platform.
- Mutually exclusive w
ith other skin plugins (all write `data-dsh-skin`) — keep one enabled at a time.
## Development
No build step: `client.js` is a browser-loadable module (`window.__ModuleLoader__.load`) with the CS
tep: `client.js` is a browser-loadable module (`window.__ModuleLoader__.load`) with the CSS inlined.
